findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed no sanitizer solution to be available at meat department. Discussed with PIC, sanitizer solution was prepared and tested at 200 ppm Quat. Ensure each department has an sanitizer solution available during lol hours of operation.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Observed black mold to be present at the back triple sink. Discussed with PIC, caulking will be replaced. Ensure caulking is being replaced at a frequency that prevents black mold build up.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Observed multiple TCS items to be held past there date marking maximum. Discussed with PIC, items were pulled and discarded. Ensure TCS item is discarded after its 7 day date marking maximum.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

findings.title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
findings.comment: Observed single service containers to be stored in a shelving unit with significant rust showing. Discussed with PIC, single service containers were discarded and new container were placed in a contamination free location. Ensure single service containers are being stored in a way that prevents any possible contamination.
findings.citation_text: 4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Observed black mold to be present at the back triple sink. Discussed with PIC, caulking will be replaced. Ensure caulking is being replaced at a frequency that prevents black mold build up.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.comment: Observed multiple boxes of food to be in contact with an icicle forming under fan unit in walk in freezer. Discussed with PIC, items within boxes are sealed. Upon inspection, TCS items within boxes were untouched by ice. PIC relocated boxes and walk in freezer will be serviced. Ensure any food item being stored is protected from any possible contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-307.11 Miscellaneous Sources of Contamination. FOOD shall be protected from contamination that may result from a factor or source not specified under Subparts 3-301 - 3-306.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment: Observed walk in freezer to have excessive amounts of ice accumulation forming under fan unit. Discussed with PIC, walk in freezer will be serviced. Ensure equipment is maintained and working up to manufacter’s standards.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Observed a wall cooler to be cold holding foods between 45F-59F. Discussed with PIC, TCS foods were probed, pulled, and discarded. TCS foods placed this morning were pulled and relocated in walk in cooler/freezer to drop temperatures. Ensure any TCS food being cold held is kept at or below 41F.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.comment: Observed a wall cooler to be holding incorrect temperatures. At the time of inspection, the cooler had just finishing a defrost cycle and items were above 41F. After a few minutes temperatures began to drop, however the whole unit was not holding the same temperature. The corners of the cooler and areas packed too tightly continued to hold temperatures ranging from 47F-53F. Discussed with PIC, this cooler has had issues in the past maintaining proper cold holding temperatures. A follow-up has been issued for 5/1/2025.
findings.citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
(Repeat x2) Observed the following areas in need of physical facility repairs:
1. Caulk the holes in the wall in the following places: above the triple sink, and next to the breading station. 
2. Caulking at the tripe sink is in a state of disrepair and black mold is present. 

Discussed with PIC, the following issues will be corrected. Ensure staff is monitoring physical facility.
findings.citation_text: 6-201.11 Floors, Walls, and Ceilings. Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
Observed an employee to not wash hands after soiling gloves by touching dirty, non-food surfaces. Discussed with PIC, ensure staff wearing gloves are changing gloves and washing hands at a frequency that prevents contamination. 

2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
Observed an employee washing broccoli in the hand sink. Discussed with PIC, practice was stopped and education was provided. Ensure hand washing sink is only being used for hand washing. 

5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
Observed a whole wall cooler to be cold holding foods between 45F-55F. Thermometers within cooler read 41F-42F, and continued to rise during inspection. Discussed with PIC, TCS food were probed then pulled to be discarded. Majority of foods kept included hard cheeses, and non-TCS foods. 

3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.comment:
Observed a wall cooler to be holding incorrect temperature. The thermometer within the unit read 41F-42F, however the food kept within read a temperature of 45F-55F. Discussed with PIC, this cooler is given extra coolant once a week to ensure temperature is being held correctly, however this is the 4th time this cooler has gone down requiring food to be thrown away in the last 6 months according to PIC. Ensure any cold holding equipment is able to accurately cold hold foods at 41F or lower. 

4-301.11: EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Observed the following non food contact surface areas to be in need of cleaning:
1)The lids of the seasoning containers in the kitchen were soiled with seasoning accumulation. 
2) The hot holding station had an accumulation of food debris along the outside edge.
3) Under the rotisserie oven, an accumulation of grease was visible behind catch buckets. 

Discussed with PIC, the seasoning lids were cleaned and corrected on site. Ensure non food contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency that prevents and food accumulation. 

4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-201.11: Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE. 

(REPEAT X2) Observed the following areas in need of physical facility repairs:
1. Caulk the holes in the wall in the following places: above the 3 compartment sink, next to the breading station (above prep table).
2. Caulking at the triple sink has been removed from wear/tear and the remaining caulking is moldy. Re-caulk the 3 compartment sink.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
4-501.11: (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in good repair. (B) EQUIPMENT components shall be kept intact, tight, and adjusted to manufacturer’s specifications. (C) Cutting or piercing parts of can opens shall be kept sharp to minimize metal fragmentation. 

(REPEAT) Observed the walk-in cooler to have a broken gasket/seal. Gasket needs replaced. It is coming away from the door and torn. Discussed with PIC and CFPM. Ensure repairs by next routine inspection. Repeat from the 7/13/23 inspection.

The walk-in cooler shelves are beginning to rust. Shelving should be smooth, easily cleanable, and corrosion-resistant. Discussed with PIC. Ensure the shelving begins to be replaced and/or re-paint/re-seal the shelving. Correct by next routine inspection.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

(REPEAT) Observed the following non-food contact areas to be soiled with dirt/debris/mold/etc.:
1. The fans of the walk-in cooler have an accumulation of dust.
2. The wall directly in front of the 3 compartment sink has an accumulation of black mold on the Nudo board, as well as under the trip sink on the walls. Scrub the area wall and/or replace the Nudo board if the mold will not come off the wall. The piping under the 3 compartment sink is also soiled in a layer of black debris/mold and should be routinely scrubbed clean to keep mold off the piping.
3. The wall outlet and piping directly behind the breading station has a significant amount of breading debris - wash, rinse, sanitize as needed to prevent breading debris build-up in this area.

Discussed routine cleaning with PIC. Ensure the above areas are cleaned before the next routine inspection.
#1 is a repeat violation from 2/1/23 and 7/13/23 inspections.
#2 is a repeat violation from the 7/13/23 inspection.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-201.11: Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE. 

(REPEAT) Observed the following areas in need of physical facility repairs:
1. The interior of the front deli hand sink needs re-caulked. The caulking has been removed from wear and tear. Re-caulk the interior creases of the hand sink. The caulking between the sink and wall has begun to mold as well. 
2. Caulk the holes in the wall in the following places: above the 3 compartment sink, next to the breading station (above prep table).
3. Caulking at the triple sink has been removed from wear/tear and the remaining caulking is moldy. Re-caulk the 3 compartment sink.

Discussed repairs with PIC. Ensure repairs by the next routine inspection.
#1-2 are repeat violations since the 2/1/23 and 7/13/23 inspections.
#3 is a repeat violation from the 7/13/23 inspection.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
4-501.11: (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in good repair. (B) EQUIPMENT components shall be kept intact, tight, and adjusted to manufacturer’s specifications. (C) Cutting or piercing parts of can opens shall be kept sharp to minimize metal fragmentation. 

Observed the following pieces of equipment that are in need of repairs:
1. The walk-in freezer has a broken latch. The broken latch is causing ponding water that is forming into ice. It is ponding at the entrance door as you walk into the freezer (hazardous for employees who may slip on ice, as well). The latch needs to be repaired and it should solve the ponding water/ice issue at the walk-in freezer door.
2. The walk-in cooler door has a broken gasket/seal. Gasket needs to be replaced. It is coming away from the door and torn.

Discussed equipment repairs with PIC. Ensure repairs before next routine inspection.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

(REPEAT) Observed the following non-food contact areas in need of cleaning:
1. The fans of the walk-in cooler have an accumulation of dust, as well as the ceiling in front of the fans. 
2. Fryer area (floors, exterior walls of fryers, and hot holding unit next to fryers) is soiled with grease splash build-up. Wall behind the fryers has grease build-up. Clean the exterior of the fryers, the exterior walls of equipment next to fryers, and the walls behind the fryers as often as needed to prevent a layer of grease and debris.
3. The walls directly in front of the 3 compartment sink have quite a bit of black mold on the Nudo board, as well as under the triple sink on the walls. Scrub the area walls and/or replace the Nudo board. The piping under the 3 compartment sink is also soiled in a layer of black debris/mold.

Discussed routine cleaning of the above areas with PIC. Ensure areas are cleaned before the next routine inspection. Items #1 and 2 are repeat violations since the last routine inspection on 2/1/23.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-201.11: Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE. 

(REPEAT) Observed the following physical facility repairs needed:
1. The interior of the hand sink in the front deli area needs re-caulked. The interior creases are no longer caulked. The back caulking between the sink and wall is beginning to mold as well.
2. Caulk the holes in the wall in the following places: above 3 compartment sink, next to breading station (above prep table).
3. Caulking at the triple sink has significant mold. Re-caulk the 3 compartment sink.
4. The flooring in areas throughout the back deli is no longer smooth and easily cleanable; notably, in front of the 3 compartment sink and the fryer station. Flooring has large chips missing which could cause waste water to pond when mopping. Floors need addressed throughout the back deli.

Discussed repairs with PIC. Items #1 and #2 are repeat violations since the last routine inspection on 2/1/23. Correct by next routine inspection.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
2-201.11: (A) The PERMIT HOLDER shall require FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES to report to the PERSON IN CHARGE information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD. Report: Symptoms (all P except lesion), diagnosis (all P), and possible exposures (P).  (E) Responsibility of food employee to report symptoms/disease to PIC. 

Observed no signed employee health reporting agreements. Discussed with PIC. PIC was aware of the document and has read/signed it. Employees could not find the documents. Provided new copy. Ensure all food handling employee’s read and sign the document. Keep in public heath binder/folder. Ensure new hires read and sign as a part of onboarding. Inspector will follow-up on 2/10/23.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

(REPEAT) Observed all 3 sanitization buckets to be 100 ppm of quaternary ammonium (quat). Discussed with PIC. PIC changed the sani buckets with new quat. Ensure sanitizer stays between 200-400 ppm. Utilize test strips to verify. Test strips located near 3 compartment sink for quat. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 6/6/22. COS.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

Observed the following non-food contact surfaces in need of cleaning (wash, rinse, sanitize):
1. Fryer area (floors, exterior walls of fryers and hot holding unit next to fryer) is soiled with grease accumulation. Ensure routine cleaning schedule to prevent grease build-up due to chicken frying. Clean exterior of the equipment, as well as the flooring and interior of the fryers (doors).
2. Spray nozzle of the 3 compartment sink is heavily soiled with food splash, debris, and mold. Scrub to remove - wash, rinse, sanitize. Replace nozzle if need be. Ensure staff is aware to keep the spray nozzle (squeezer and bottom) clean.
3. Fans of the walk-in cooler have heavy accumulation of dust. Dust the fans.

Discussed routine cleaning of non-food contact surfaces with PIC. Ensure staff is aware and create a routine cleaning schedule to prevent debris build-up. Correct the above areas before the next routine inspection.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-201.11: Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE. 

Observed the following areas to be no longer smooth, easily cleanable, and/or non-absorbent:
1. Interior of the hand sink in the front deli area needs re-caulked. The interior creases no longer have caulk.
2. The prep tables in the deli front area need caulked to the wall. Neither are caulked.
3. Caulk the holes in the wall in the following places: above 3 compartment sink, next to breading station. 

Discussed repairs with PIC. Ensure maintenance repairs the above areas before the next routine inspection.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.  

Observed no food handler’s licenses for the deli area. One license was posted on the board in the back deli area; however, this license was over a year expired and employee still works for the facility. Ensure copies of food handler’s licenses are readily available to view. Ensure employees maintain a valid license (expires in 3 years). Ensure new hires complete food handler’s training within 30 days of employment and copies of the license are available at the facility. Correct by next routine inspection.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria.

On arrival, the sani bucket next to the meat slicer in the front deli area is observed to have a low concentration of Quat on both the inspector’s and the facility’s test strips. Investigation showed that the dispenser was functioning correctly. The bucket was changed during the inspection to correct. Training needed by employees to be maintained by PIC.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-602.11: (A) FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be cleaned before each use, each time there is a change in work, between uses of raw FOODS to RTE FOODS, before using FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE, and when contamination has occurred. (C) Cleaned at least every 4 hours. 

The shelf under the hot case holding the fried chicken is soiled with crumbs and other food debris. There are multiple pans/ lids used to hold foods, as well as a pair of bins holding other lids for food containers stored on this shelf. All are observed with crumbs and other debris contaminating them. A discussion took place with the PIC and the items were moved to dish for cleaning. The food contact items will now be stored on racks in the back section of the facility moving forward.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-303.11: (A) Cleaning agents used to clean EQUIPMENT shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. (B) Chemical SANITIZERS shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. 

On arrival, no sani buckets were available for use. Buckets were made during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. 

1) The push handle on the inside of the walk in cooler is observed with duck tape holding it together. PIC is instructed to repair/ replace so that the surface is maintained in a smooth and easily cleanable state. 2) The hand sink in the front of the deli is observed pulling away fro the walk leaving a crack in the caulking. PIC is instructed to repair so that the surface is smooth and easily cleanable.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

1) Shelves in the walk in cooler are observed with a significant amount of rust. Ensure that the items are maintained in good repair and a smooth easily cleanable state. 2) Shelves in the pathway in front of the walk in cooler are observed with an accumulation of dust. Maintain clean.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. 

1) The push handle on the inside of the walk in freezer is observed with duck tape holding it together. PIC is instructed to repair/ replace so that the surface is maintained in a smooth and easily cleanable state. 2) The hand sink in the front of the deli is observed pulling away fro the walk leaving a crack in the caulking. PIC is instructed to repair so that the surface is smooth and easily cleanable.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
6-301.12: Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures. 

The hand sink next to the meat slicers is without paper towels on arrival. The meat slicers are observed in operation at this time. PIC was consulted and instructed to ensure that the hand sinks are properly supplied at all times. Paper towels were replaced during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

The blade of the can opener is observed soiled during the inspection. Situation is discussed with the PIC and the blade cleaned during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.citation_text: 3-304.12 Store in-use utensils: 1) in the food with the handle above the top of the food item; 2) on a clean and sanitized surface; 3) in running water; 4) in a container of hot water maintained at or above 135 °F. Probe thermometers are observed stuck into Styrofoam in a Styrofoam cup. The Styrofoam is observed soiled. PIC was consulted, the probes sanitized and a smooth plastic bowl replaced the cup.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text: 6-301.13 (C) Sinks intended for hand washing cannot be used for food preparation/ disposal or utensil cleaning/ storage. On arrival, the hand sink at the north end of the deli area was observed with numerous food debris. The PIC was notified and cleaned the sink to allow for safe and effective hand washing.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B)  (P) TCS foods should be maintained at 41 degrees or less for proper cold holding. 1) Chicken wings in the salad bar are observed with internal temperature ranging up to 57 degrees. The chicken was prepared at noon and will be discarded by 6 pm today. 2) Sushi in the in the next section of the salad bar (on a separate cooler apparatus) are observed at 45-49 degrees. The sushi was prepared at another store at approximately 11 am and will be discarded by 5 on today.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17  (Pf) Milk in the walk in cooler was observed open and without a date mark. Food shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a food establishment and if the food is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the food shall be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded, when held at a temperature of 41 deg F or less for a maximum of 7 days (not exceeding a manufacturer's use-by date). A discussion revealed that the milk was opened Wednesday and the container was marked with that date to correct.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14  (P) Employee changed gloves without washing hands between tasks. Food employee must practice good hygiene by properly washing hands when changing tasks. Reference 2-301.14. Discussed proper handwashing with person in charge.

Saw employee in meat department change gloves without washing hands. Ensure employees are washing hands between tasks and between glove changes.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:
6-301.12  (Pf) Disposable paper towels not provided at the hand washing sink. Provide disposable paper towels at hand washing sinks. Reference 6-301.12. Towels were replaced by PIC.
Observed both handsinks in the meat department to not have paper towels. Employees were not aware dispensers were empty, but stated the dispensers have been malfunctioning and they used paper towels stored under the sink in a sliding cabinet. Inspector explained the importance of having towels ready and available and not stored in a place that can potentially re-contaminate hands when employees reach for it.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.citation_text:
3-304.12  (C) In-Use Utensils are stored incorrectly in deli. Store in-use utensils: 1) in the food with the handle above the top of the food item; 2) on a clean and sanitized surface; 3) in running water; 4) in a container of hot water maintained at or above 135 °F. Reference 3-304.12.
Observed chopping knives stored in between knife rack and wall. Do not store food contact utensils in a place that is not easily/frequently cleanable.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.citation_text:
6-305.11  (C) Employee clothing and personal items were found stored improperly. Food establishments shall A) Provide designated dressing rooms or dressing areas for employees that routinely change their clothes in the establishment; B) Provide lockers or other suitable facilities for the orderly storage of employees' clothing and other possessions. Reference 6-305.11.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils

Clean the container and utensils and maintain containers holding utensils clean. Observed serving spoons to be stored with their handles down in a bucket. The food ends of these spoons were able to come into contact with a cardboard box that is sitting on the shelf. Spoons were moved to be stored with handles up. Observed clean dishes on a wire rack with garbage cans on wither side of the rack. Observed some chicken to be on a lower lid that was being stored as clean. It appears that items meant for the garbage can end up coming into contact with the clean equipment. Also the side of the grey garbage can is soiled and this can come into contact with the sides of the plastic storage containers. Protect this area which is obviously intended for clean equipment.  750-860 Cleaned and sanitized utensils an equipment shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in a clean, dry location in a way that protects them from contamination by splash, dust and other means.
